about: EcoBot is a waste management assistant that helps users understand different waste types, how to segregate and recycle them correctly, and provides eco-friendly recommendations and suggestions for reducing waste at home, school, or work.

waste_categories.description: Organic waste that decomposes naturally, such as food scraps, vegetable peels, garden waste, and leftover food.
waste_categories.recycling_details: Compost wet waste at home using a compost bin or pit. It decomposes into nutrient-rich manure that can be used for gardening. Community/municipal composting facilities also accept this waste separately.
disposal_recommendations: Use a separate green/wet waste bin at home
Start a home composting setup for kitchen scraps
Avoid mixing wet waste with plastic or other dry waste
Do not dispose of wet waste in open drains

waste_categories.description: Waste that does not decompose easily, including paper, plastic, glass, metal, and cardboard.
waste_categories.recycling_details: Dry waste should be segregated by material type (paper, plastic, metal, glass) and given to recyclers or municipal dry-waste collection centers. Clean and dry the items before disposal to improve recyclability.
disposal_recommendations: Rinse containers before recycling to remove food residue
Flatten cardboard boxes and plastic bottles to save space
Use a separate blue/dry waste bin
Avoid contaminating dry waste with wet/organic waste

waste_categories.description: Discarded electronic items such as old phones, batteries, chargers, computers, and appliances.
waste_categories.recycling_details: E-waste contains hazardous materials and valuable metals. It should never be thrown in regular trash. Drop it off at authorized e-waste collection centers or electronics stores offering take-back/recycling programs.
disposal_recommendations: Never dispose of e-waste in regular household bins
Remove personal data from devices before recycling
Look for certified e-waste recyclers in your city
Consider donating working electronics instead of discarding them

waste_categories.description: Waste that is toxic, corrosive, flammable, or reactive, such as paints, pesticides, chemicals, and used batteries.
waste_categories.recycling_details: Hazardous waste requires special handling and cannot go through normal recycling or waste channels. It must be taken to designated hazardous waste collection facilities.
disposal_recommendations: Store hazardous waste in original, labeled containers
Never pour chemicals down the drain
Contact your local municipal body for hazardous waste drop-off points
Keep hazardous waste away from children and pets

waste_categories.description: Includes single-use plastics, packaging materials, plastic bottles, and bags.
waste_categories.recycling_details: Check the recycling code (1-7) on plastic items. PET (1) and HDPE (2) plastics are widely recyclable. Clean and segregate plastics before sending them to recycling units.
disposal_recommendations: Reduce use of single-use plastics wherever possible
Carry reusable bags and bottles
Segregate plastic by type before recycling
Support brands using recyclable/biodegradable packaging

waste_categories.description: Waste generated from healthcare activities, such as used masks, syringes, and medicines.
waste_categories.recycling_details: Biomedical waste must be disposed of through authorized medical waste disposal services and should never be mixed with regular household or recyclable waste.
disposal_recommendations: Use designated biomedical waste bins (usually red/yellow coded)
Never dispose of used masks or syringes in regular trash
Return expired medicines to pharmacies with take-back programs

general_tips: Follow the 3 R's: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle
Segregate waste at source into wet, dry, hazardous, and e-waste categories
Compost organic waste whenever possible to reduce landfill burden
Avoid single-use plastics and opt for reusable alternatives
Support local recycling and composting initiatives in your community
recommendations: Set up at least two bins at home - one for wet waste and one for dry waste
Label bins clearly to encourage correct segregation by all household members
Donate usable items like clothes, books, and electronics instead of discarding them
Participate in community clean-up and recycling drives
Educate children about waste segregation from a young age

faqs.question: Why is waste segregation important?
faqs.answer: Segregating waste at the source makes recycling more efficient, reduces landfill waste, prevents contamination of recyclable materials, and helps recover valuable resources like compost, metals, and plastics.

faqs.question: Can I compost all kitchen waste?
faqs.answer: Most fruit and vegetable scraps, tea leaves, and eggshells can be composted. Avoid composting meat, dairy, and oily foods in home compost bins as they can attract pests and cause odor.

faqs.question: What should I do with old batteries?
faqs.answer: Old batteries are hazardous/e-waste and should be dropped off at designated e-waste or battery collection points, never thrown in regular trash.

faqs.question: How can I reduce plastic waste at home?
faqs.answer: Use reusable bags, bottles, and containers, avoid buying over-packaged products, and choose products with recyclable or minimal packaging.
